newsitem.title: USA: Air Force suspends Zenith Data computer orders.
newsitem.headline: Air Force suspends Zenith Data computer orders.
newsitem.dateline: MAXWELL AIR FORCE BASE, GUNTER ANNEX, Ala. 1997-04-02

text.p: The U.S. Air Force Wednesday said it had immediately suspended all government computer orders from Zenith Data Systems.

When the contract was announced in 1996, officials said it was worth nearly $1 billion. Under terms of the original contract, Zenith, a unit of Packard Bell would compete with General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp to supply personal computers and related equipment to the Air Force. A spokeswoman said the decision to suspend the Zenith portion of the contract does not affect Hughes.

Robert Frye, executive director of the Air Force's Standard Systems Group, said the suspension was based on Zenith Data Systems' failure to sustain an acceptable level of performance on delivery and warranty.
He also stated no new orders will be placed with Zenith Data at this time.

"Our prime concern is our government and Air Force customer," Frye said. "ZDS remains under contractual obligation to complete delivery on existing orders, and provide warranty service for five years and software upgrades for three years," Frye said.

The Zenith Data delivery orders currently at the Air Force Central Order Processing Office, as well as orders in the pipeline will be returned immediately to the appropriate issuing contracting offices, the Air Force said.
The move is the second time the Air Force has suspended its contract with Zenith Data. The spokeswoman said the Air Force could life the suspension if Zenith Data resolved the performance issues.

In a statement, Zenith said it has worked to improve the volume deliveries to the Air Force as agreed to under the Desktop V contract and it has prepared "an agressive and attractive proposal to offer the government the latest technology at unsurpassed prices."
The company said the proposal is still under review by the Air Force.
